nary_nodes.label: Release of GTA 6 on 2026-11-19
evidence: GTA 6 will be released on 19 November - and with Rockstar recently opening up pre-orders, this date seems all but certain.
Rockstar said players who pre-order will be able to begin pre-loading it on their consoles on 12 November to ensure they are able to play at launch.

nary_nodes.label: GTA 6 pre-orders available from 2026-06-25
evidence: GTA 6 became available to pre-order at midnight on 25 June in the UK and elsewhere around the world, after Rockstar revealed the game's pre-sales launch date and cover art in mid-June.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Example 'GTA 6 pre-orders available from 2026-06-25' represents a sales promotion, matching schema.org's SaleEvent.

nary_nodes.label: GTA 6 delayed from 2025-09-01 to 2026-05-01
evidence: But it was delayed twice previously, from autumn 2025 and May 2026.
In a statement when the second delay was announced, Rockstar said it needed extra months to finish the game with the level of polish fans had come to 'expect and deserve'.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Example 'GTA 6 delayed from 2025-09-01 to 2026-05-01' describes a date change, not directly covered by schema.org candidates.

nary_nodes.label: Analysts estimate GTA 6 development cost exceeds $1bn
evidence: Analysts believe Rockstar's action adventure could become the most expensive game ever made, with estimates putting development costs at more than $1bn (£866m).

It has also seen some issues since, including accusations of 'union-busting' by sacked workers at Rockstar North, its Edinburgh HQ, where developers have been racing to get GTA 6 ready for release in November.

nary_nodes.label: GTA 6 gameplay footage leaked in 2026
evidence: Several months later, footage and images leaked after teenage hackers targeted the company.

nary_nodes.label: Vic Hood claims GTA games are culturally relevant
evidence: She added that the games were also 'extremely culturally relevant' too.

'Rockstar has always had its finger on the pulse of music, entertainment, societal, political, celebrity, and online culture trends, and they've never shied away from satirising these things in GTA games,' she said.

nary_nodes.label: Sir Ian Livingstone calls GTA bigger than film/song
evidence: British gaming entrepreneur Sir Ian Livingstone told the BBC's Today programme that the series, originally developed in Scotland, was 'bigger than any film or song' and an 'incredible achievement in interactive software'.
